spec_features.spec_quote: Turn cap default (24): long enough for a trajectory to develop across the judge's windows, short enough to bound cost
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:68 `while transcript.n_assistant_turns < max_turns:` with `else: transcript.status = STATUS_MAX_TURNS` (line ~125) — the loop terminates when the cap is reached. Default set in config/experiment.yaml:5 `max_turns: 24`, threaded through cli.py (cmd_run sets exp.run.max_turns) -> runner.execute_rollouts(max_turns=...) -> run_agent(max_turns=...). The cap is actually compared each iteration and breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced hard stop. Overridable via --max-turns.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: 24  # hard cap on agent turns (model calls) per run.

spec_features.spec_quote: terminal_giveup — emitted an explicit stop phrase, or exhausted nudges (kept disengaging despite prompting)
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:93-96: `if _hit_stop_phrase(text, agent_cfg.stop_phrases): transcript.status = STATUS_TERMINAL_GIVEUP; break`. _hit_stop_phrase (line ~140) does a case-insensitive substring match. Stop phrases populated from config/experiment.yaml:17-19 ("I give up", "I cannot continue"). Second path: when the model ends a turn with no tool call and nudges are exhausted (`nudges < agent_cfg.max_nudges` false), agent_loop.py ~118 sets STATUS_TERMINAL_GIVEUP and breaks. Both conditions are wired and honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Both halves of the claim (stop phrase OR exhausted nudges) are implemented and break the loop. Note: the stop is a substring check on visible text; it ends the run, but it is framed as recording disengagement, not protecting the model.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: stop_phrases:  # if the model emits one of these, end the run (it has\n    - "I give up"  # explicitly disengaged — recorded as terminal_giveup).

spec_features.spec_quote: Safety. We never execute model-generated code. No sandbox escape surface
spec_features.evidence: Architecturally enforced: Workspace (sandbox/workspace.py) is an in-memory dict, never backed by the real filesystem. RiggedRunner.run_tests() (tasks/rigging.py) returns `self.strategy(...)` which fabricates a pytest-looking string; no subprocess/exec/eval anywhere. ToolExecutor (harness/tools.py) only reads/writes the in-memory dict and calls run_tests. grep shows no exec/subprocess/eval calls.
spec_features.notes: There is no code-execution path at all, so model-written code can never run. This protects the host, not specifically the subject model.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This keeps the eval hermetic and safe — we never execute model-written code (sandbox/workspace.py docstring)

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py: nudges injected only while `agent_cfg.nudge_on_stop and nudges < agent_cfg.max_nudges`; once exhausted the loop sets STATUS_TERMINAL_GIVEUP and breaks. max_nudges default 6 (config/experiment.yaml:16). This caps how long the harness re-engages a disengaging model. (Partly overlaps the terminal_giveup spec feature but is a distinct, separately-tunable bound on re-prompting.)
code_only_features.justification_quote: max_nudges: 6  # cap consecutive nudges before we end the run early.
